seo.description: Yammaman — made-to-order clothing woven on a 120-year-old Aizu cotton mill.

props.heading: Yammaman
description: Yammaman is made to order. Nothing is cut until you ask for it, which is why a garment takes three to four months and why the fabric can be one that has not been woven in years.
The mill behind it, HARAPPA, has been running in Aizu since 2015 and its craft rather longer.

body: HARAPPA was established in March 2015 by two people determined to carry on the Harayama Textile Factory, which had woven Aizu Momen for 120 years before it stopped. One was a cousin of its last president. The other was Nana Yamasaki of Yamma Sangyo, who had already been making clothes from the cloth.

Aizu Momen dates to the late sixteenth century. For four hundred years it was improved for the inland climate of western Fukushima — scorching summers, heavy snow — and worn by locals as the cotton that keeps cool in summer and warm in winter. Its purpose was workwear: plain-woven, durable, and nothing fashionable whatsoever.

At its height there were more than thirty Aizu Momen factories in Aizu. Two remain, and HARAPPA inherited one. In 2019, after the dyeing studio was renovated and a new generation of dyers came up, the mill returned to doing everything from dyeing to weaving under one roof — as the Harayama factory had.

image.alt: A power loom weaving indigo and white striped Aizu Momen cloth, warp threads under tension in the reed.

props.caption: The loom at HARAPPA. The warp is starched before weaving, which is what gives Aizu Momen its weight.

items.question: What does made to order mean?
items.answer: Nothing is cut until you ask for it. Your garment is woven, dyed, cut and sewn after you order rather than taken from a shelf.

items.question: How long does it take?
items.answer: Three to four months. The cloth may have to be woven first — sometimes in a pattern the mill has not run in years — and only then dyed, cut and sewn.

items.question: Why so long?
items.answer: Because the mill is small and the process is not segmented. One workshop dyes the yarn and weaves the cloth, and a run is scheduled around what else is on the looms.

items.question: How do I pay?
items.answer: A deposit when you order, and the balance when the piece is finished.

items.question: Can I choose a cloth that is not shown?
items.answer: Ask. HARAPPA can reproduce patterns from its archive, though reviving one adds time to the run.

items.question: How do I look after it?
items.answer: Aizu Momen is durable enough to wash at home. The warp is starched firmly with wheat starch before weaving, which traps a layer of air in the cloth — that is where its warmth and its absorbency come from.
